topics: 🕍 A Time of Favor — why praying with the congregation is a prayer God never despises
🏃 Early and Late to the Synagogue — the elders of Babylonia and Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi's advice to his sons
🔍 'The Time of Finding' — a wife, Torah, death, burial, or a lavatory?
📏 Four Cubits of Halakha — where God's presence rests since the Temple was destroyed
📜 Shnayim Mikra — completing the Torah portion with the congregation, twice text and once translation
🌅 Rabban Gamliel's Ruling — the halakha follows him, and Shema twice around dawn

overview.title: 📖 Overview: The Synagogue, the Study Hall, and the Torah Portion
overview.subtitle: Berakhot 8a–8b
overview.hebrewSource: אֵימָתַי עֵת רָצוֹן — בְּשָׁעָה שֶׁהַצִּבּוּר מִתְפַּלְּלִין
overview.label: The scene:
overview.text: The daf opens by defining the 'time of favor' in Psalms 69:14 as the hour when the congregation prays — God never despises the prayer of the many. Reish Lakish calls one who has a synagogue and does not enter it an 'evil neighbor', and the long lives of Babylonia's elders are credited to arriving early and leaving late. A playful chain of interpretations reads 'the time of finding' as a wife, Torah, death, burial, or a lavatory. Rav Ḥisda's teachings on the synagogue lead to Ulla's famous line that since the Temple's destruction God has only the four cubits of halakha, which changed where Abaye prayed. The amud ends with the obligation to complete the weekly portion with the congregation. Amud bet continues with Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi's and Rava's advice to their sons, the caveats on passing behind a synagogue, praise of the Medes and Persians, and finally a return to the mishna: the halakha follows Rabban Gamliel, and Rabbi Shimon ben Yoḥai's case of reciting Shema twice around dawn.

slides.title: 🕍 Why Pray With the Congregation?
slides.subtitle: The prayer of the many is never despised

nodes.content: ❓ 'Let my prayer be unto You, Lord, in a time of favor' (Psalms 69:14) — when is a עֵת רָצוֹן?

✅ When the congregation is praying. Rabbi Yosei son of Rabbi Ḥanina: 'In a time of acceptance I have answered you' (Isaiah 49:8). Rabbi Aḥa: 'God is mighty, He despises no one' (Job 36:5) + 'for there were many with me' (Psalms 55:19)
📜 Rabbi Natan's baraita: God says — whoever engages in Torah, acts of kindness, and prays with the congregation, I credit him as if he redeemed Me and My children from among the nations

columns.label: Reish Lakish
columns.content: One with a synagogue in his city who does not enter to pray is an 'evil neighbor' (Jeremiah 12:14) and causes exile for himself and his children

columns.label: R' Yoḥanan
columns.content: Puzzled that there are elders in Babylonia, since long life is promised 'upon the land' — until told they go early and late to the synagogue: that is what helped them

nodes.content: 🏃 Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi to his sons: 'Go early and go late and enter the synagogue, so that your lives will be extended' — 'watching daily at My gates… whoso finds Me finds life' (Proverbs 8:34–35)

callout.label: Rav Ḥisda:
callout.text: A person should always enter 'two doorways' into the synagogue. Not literally — rather, walk in the distance of two doorways and only then pray.

slides.title: 🔍 What Is 'The Time of Finding'?
slides.subtitle: 'For this, let every pious man pray to You in the time of finding' (Psalms 32:6) — six readings
rows: 'He who finds a wife finds good' (Proverbs 18:22) — in Eretz Yisrael they asked a groom: matza or motzeh ('more bitter than death', Ecclesiastes 7:26)?
Death — pray for an easy one
'Issues [totzaot] of death' (Psalms 68:21); 903 kinds of death — the hardest is croup, the easiest the kiss, like drawing a hair from milk
'Glad when they can find a grave' (Job 3:22); Rabba bar Rav Sheila: pray for mercy until the last shovelful
In the West they said: this explanation is the best of all

callout.label: Method:
callout.text: Each sage anchors 'finding' (מְצֹא) to another verse with the same root, showing how one word can hold a whole range of human needs worth praying for.

slides.title: 📏 Four Cubits of Halakha
slides.subtitle: Rava asks Rafram bar Pappa for Rav Ḥisda's teachings on the synagogue

lines.speaker: Rav Ḥisda
lines.text: 'The Lord loves the gates of Zion more than all the dwellings of Jacob' (Psalms 87:2) — He loves gates distinguished (הַמְצוּיָּינִים) by halakha more than synagogues and study halls.

lines.speaker: Ulla
lines.text: Since the day the Temple was destroyed, the Holy One has nothing in His world but the אַרְבַּע אַמּוֹת שֶׁל הֲלָכָה, the four cubits of halakha alone.

lines.speaker: Abaye
lines.text: At first I studied at home and prayed in the synagogue. Once I heard Ulla's teaching, I pray only where I study.

lines.speaker: Gemara
lines.text: Rabbi Ami and Rabbi Asi had thirteen synagogues in Tiberias, yet prayed only between the pillars where they studied.

lines.speaker: Ulla
lines.text: One who benefits from his own labor is greater than one who merely fears Heaven: of the God-fearing it says only 'happy is the man' (Psalms 112:1); of the laborer, 'you are happy and it is good for you' (Psalms 128:2) — happy in this world, good in the World-to-Come.

lines.speaker: Ulla
lines.text: One should always live where his teacher lives — as long as Shimi ben Gera lived, Solomon did not marry Pharaoh's daughter. The baraita saying not to live near one's teacher speaks of a student who will not submit to him.

callout.label: Leaving during Torah reading:
callout.text: 'They who forsake the Lord will perish' (Isaiah 1:28) — this is one who leaves while the Torah scroll is out. Rabbi Abbahu would leave between readers; Rav Pappa asked about between verses, and the question stands (teiku). Rav Sheshet turned away and studied: 'we are engaged in ours, they in theirs'.

slides.title: 📜 Complete the Portion With the Congregation
slides.subtitle: Rabbi Ami's rule and the story of Rav Beivai bar Abaye

steps.content: 1️⃣ Rav Huna bar Yehuda in the name of Rabbi Ami: always complete your portions with the congregation — שְׁנַיִם מִקְרָא וְאֶחָד תַּרְגּוּם, twice the text and once the translation
2️⃣ Even a verse like 'Atarot and Divon' (Numbers 32:3), which is only place names — and the reward is that one's days and years are extended
3️⃣ Rav Beivai bar Abaye planned to catch up on the whole year's portions on the eve of Yom Kippur

4️⃣ Ḥiyya bar Rav of Difti stopped him: 'You shall afflict your souls on the ninth' (Leviticus 23:32) — but the fast is on the tenth! Rather, one who eats and drinks on the ninth is credited as if he fasted on both the ninth and the tenth
5️⃣ He then thought to read the portions early; an elder taught him: neither earlier nor later than the congregation

6️⃣ Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi to his sons: complete your portions with the congregation; be careful with the jugular veins in slaughter like Rabbi Yehuda; and respect an elder who forgot his learning through no fault of his own — the tablets and the broken tablets both rest in the Ark

callout.label: Rava to his sons:
callout.text: Do not cut meat on your hand (danger, or spoiling the meal); do not sit on the bed of an Aramean woman (read as: do not sleep without Shema, do not marry a convert, or literally — after Rav Pappa found a dead baby under such a bed); and do not pass behind a synagogue while the congregation prays.

slides.title: 🌅 Back to the Mishna: Rabban Gamliel and Shema Around Dawn
slides.subtitle: Plus Abaye's caveats and what Rabbi Akiva and Rabban Gamliel admired in other nations

boxes.title: Halakha follows Rabban Gamliel
items: Rav Yehuda in the name of Shmuel: evening Shema may be recited until dawn
Rabbi Shimon ben Yoḥai: sometimes one recites Shema twice 'at night' — just before and just after dawn — fulfilling both the night and day obligations
Contradiction: is after dawn night or day? Answer: it is still night, but called 'day' because some people rise then
Rav Aḥa bar Ḥanina in the name of Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi: the halakha follows Rabbi Shimon ben Yoḥai

boxes.title: Passing behind a synagogue
items: Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi: forbidden while the congregation prays — it looks like contempt
Abaye's exceptions: another entrance; another synagogue in town
Also permitted if carrying a burden, running, or wearing tefillin — no one will suspect him

boxes.title: Learning from other nations
items: Rabbi Akiva likes the Medes for three things: cutting meat only on the table, kissing only the back of the hand, taking counsel only in the field (Jacob called Rachel and Leah to the field, Genesis 31:4)
Rabban Gamliel likes the Persians for three: modesty in eating, in the lavatory, and in intimate matters
Yet Rav Yosef: 'My consecrated ones' (Isaiah 13:3) — the Persians consecrated and designated for Gehenna

callout.label: Second version:
callout.text: Some attach Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi's ruling to a different baraita of Rabbi Shimon ben Yoḥai in the name of Rabbi Akiva: sometimes one recites Shema twice 'in the day', just before and just after sunrise, fulfilling both the night and day obligations — with the same internal contradiction about whether the time before sunrise is day or night.

summary.principle: The time of favor is when the congregation prays — and God's presence today rests in the four cubits of halakha, so prayer, study, and the weekly portion belong together in one place.

flowSteps.content: 🕍 'A time of favor' = when the congregation prays; God does not despise the prayer of the many
🏃 Enter the synagogue early and late → long life even in Babylonia; skipping it makes one an 'evil neighbor'
📏 Since the Temple fell, God has only the four cubits of halakha → Abaye, Rabbi Ami and Rabbi Asi pray where they study

columns.content: 📜 Complete the portion with the congregation: twice text, once translation, not early or late
🚶 Don't pass behind a synagogue during prayer — unless another door, another shul, a burden, running, or tefillin

flowSteps.content: 🎓 Key Principle: The halakha follows Rabban Gamliel — Shema until dawn — and per Rabbi Shimon ben Yoḥai, two recitations around dawn can cover both night and day

quiz.q: According to the Gemara, when is the 'time of favor' mentioned in Psalms 69:14?
o: At dawn, when people rise
When the congregation is praying
On the eve of Yom Kippur
When one studies halakha alone
quiz.e: The Gemara identifies the time of favor with the hour of communal prayer, since God does not despise the prayer of the many.

quiz.q: Why was Rabbi Yoḥanan surprised that there are elders in Babylonia, and what resolved his surprise?
o: He thought Babylonians did not study Torah; he learned they had thirteen synagogues
Long life is promised 'upon the land' of Israel; he learned they go early and late to the synagogue
He thought Babylonia was unhealthy; he learned they eat modestly like the Persians
He thought they lacked teachers; he learned they lived near their rabbis
quiz.e: Deuteronomy 11:21 promises long days 'upon the land'. When told that Babylonians arrive early and leave late from the synagogue, Rabbi Yoḥanan said that is what extended their lives.

quiz.q: What did Abaye change after hearing Ulla's teaching about the 'four cubits of halakha'?
o: He stopped studying at home
He began praying only where he studied instead of in the synagogue
He moved to live near his teacher
He started reading the Torah portion twice each week
quiz.e: Abaye said that at first he studied at home and prayed in the synagogue, but after learning that God's presence rests only in the four cubits of halakha, he prayed only where he studied.

quiz.q: Why did Ḥiyya bar Rav of Difti stop Rav Beivai bar Abaye from finishing the year's Torah portions on the eve of Yom Kippur?
o: Because Torah study is forbidden on the eve of Yom Kippur
Because the portions must be read only on Shabbat
Because one who eats and drinks on the ninth of Tishrei is credited as if he fasted both the ninth and tenth, so that day is for eating
Because the translation may not be read before the fast
quiz.e: He cited Leviticus 23:32, 'afflict your souls on the ninth', and explained that eating on the ninth counts like fasting on both days, so Yom Kippur eve is dedicated to eating and drinking.

quiz.q: In what case does Abaye permit passing behind a synagogue while the congregation is praying?
o: Only if one has already prayed that day
If there is another entrance, another synagogue, or one is carrying a burden, running, or wearing tefillin
Only on Shabbat
Never; the prohibition is absolute
quiz.e: Abaye limits the prohibition to cases where onlookers would suspect the passerby of avoiding prayer; another door, another synagogue, a burden, running, or tefillin all remove that suspicion.
